name: Alsace grand cru Altenberg de Bergheim

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Gewürztraminer is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Riesling is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Pinot Gris is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Pinot Noir is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water. Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. Granite weathers to coarse, acid, free-draining soil that warms quickly and holds heat. Its acidity tends to lower the grapes' acidity, which suits Gamay.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.
Faces the midday sun. In a climate this cool, that extra warmth is often what gets grapes fully ripe.
